format: One self-contained HTML scene, 1080×1920 — the video source, a replicable template, and this piece's shipped production context. Deterministic: renderAt(t) is a pure function of t; ?render exposes window.__seek(t) for frame capture; ?edit=1 opens the inspector.
grammar: A59 motion-graphics spine (one persistent object: the token piece, wd-token-piece) + cinematic typography rationed to the number (C1) + 2D graphics for the cut (C3); whiteboard rejected (see phase-2 style_mix).
safe_zone: Stage x[100,980], y[250,1500]; word band y[1300,1580]; furniture at y 104 stands outside the stage by design (top chrome zone).
word_layer: Monument mode during L1/L8 (40 px — the words belong to the monument), band mode otherwise (44–64 px per line). States: upcoming .32 / spoken .92 / current gold + scale 1.07 / principal words gold from their instant.

elements.name: the void
elements.rationale: The A59 ground: deep-navy radial void. Every later element is a guest on it; nothing competes with the monument or the piece.

elements.name: particle field
elements.rationale: Barely-there depth so the void reads as space, not emptiness. Deterministic (seeded) — the same field in every frame and every render.

elements.name: lane furniture
elements.home: top centre, y 104: 'EARTH ONE · WORD DEFINITIONS'
elements.rationale: The lane's standing furniture — names the series and stays out of the stage. Standing lane property, flagged in the register (R-6).

elements.name: ghost numeral '3.2'
elements.rationale: The hook's figure at monumental scale in ghost register — present as mass, not as text: the viewer FEELS the scale before the line names it. Three states: assembles in the lead-in, recedes behind the question, returns at the bookend where it expands to the full digits.

elements.name: QUADRILLION display word
elements.rationale: The figure's name in the lane's gold — the monument's second half. Cinematic typography rationed to this one word: scale is the sensation; the name is what the viewer learns to say.

elements.name: context line
elements.home: centre y 1108: 'A QUADRILLION IS A THOUSAND TRILLION'
elements.rationale: Scale context in one glanceable line, landing as the narration says 'quadrillion' — the number gets a size the viewer already owns (a trillion) without a second narration fact.

elements.name: source line
elements.home: centre y 1188–1265: 'Google processes more than 3.2 quadrillion tokens a month — Google I/O 2026'
elements.rationale: The honesty furniture: the figure's owner, scope and source on screen while the hook lands, so the monument never reads as a invented number. The verb on screen matches the narration's: 'processes'.

elements.name: question tile 'ONE TOKEN?'
elements.rationale: The unit the piece exists to define, posed as an empty outlined slot — a token-shaped hole the rest of the piece fills. Lands on the question's key word ('one'); the dashed outline is the not-yet-known register.

elements.name: THE TOKEN PIECE (persistent object)
elements.rationale: The piece's one persistent object (A59 spine). States: defined at C3 ('A CHUNK OF TEXT'), read at C4 ('THE UNIT IT READS'), miniaturized into the stream at C7 ('THE UNIT IT THINKS IN'). Its sub-label is its state; the viewer tracks ONE object through the whole argument.

elements.name: the cut word 'unhappiness'
elements.rationale: A whole word big enough to be cut in public. Chosen because its three pieces are real tokens of a mainstream tokenizer and its meaning survives the cut — the demonstration is honest, not staged with a rigged word.

elements.name: piece 'un'
elements.home: first third of the cut word
elements.rationale: A prefix that is a token on its own — the cut's first proof that pieces, not words, are the unit.

elements.name: piece 'happi'
elements.rationale: The cut's shock value: 'happi' is not an English word at all, yet it is a token — the strongest single image of the definition.

elements.name: piece 'ness'
elements.home: last third of the cut word
elements.rationale: The suffix piece completes the set; the three gold ticks under the pieces mark each as counted — pieces become units.

elements.name: scanner gate
elements.home: two gold posts at x 292 / 780, y 540–1060 + sweep line
elements.rationale: The machine's eye, staged as a gate the piece passes through: reading shown as an act performed on the unit, timed to 'It reads tokens.' The sweep is the only fast motion in the piece — the machine's moment gets the machine's tempo.

elements.name: rule chip '≈ 4 CHARACTERS EACH'
elements.rationale: The size rule as a stage prop, kept on screen while the count is set up — the viewer carries the number 4 into the count and can test it against the tiles.

elements.name: invite 'COUNT WITH ME'
elements.rationale: The invitation gets its own stage beat before the first tile lands — the viewer is recruited, not ambushed, and the suspense gap (F4) has a visual tenant.

elements.name: count tile 'The'
elements.rationale: Counted piece 1 of 5 — lands exactly on the spoken word. The tiles ARE the piece's object cut into its sentence: the count is performed on the thesis itself.

elements.name: count tile 'machine'
elements.rationale: Counted piece 2 of 5.

elements.name: count tile 'reads'
elements.rationale: Counted piece 3 of 5 — the verb at the row's centre, as in the sentence.

elements.name: count tile 'tokens'
elements.rationale: Counted piece 4 of 5.

elements.name: count tile '.' (the full stop)
elements.rationale: The fifth token is the full stop — the count's surprise and its proof of honesty: punctuation counts, which is why the answer is five and not four. Landing timed to the end of 'Tokens.' so the dot arrives as the word completes.

elements.name: the counter '1 2 3 4 5 — FIVE TOKENS'
elements.rationale: Numerals light in step with the tiles; the verdict lands on the spoken 'Five'. Two centred rows so the numerals never shift when the verdict appears — the count's arithmetic is staged as bookkeeping, not decoration.

elements.name: stake tile READS
elements.rationale: Stakes beat 1 of 4, lighting on its spoken word. The 2×2 grid gives the list a shape the viewer completes as it fills — a list performed, not recited.

elements.name: stake tile WRITES
elements.rationale: Stakes beat 2 of 4.

elements.name: stake tile YOU PAY
elements.rationale: Stakes beat 3 of 4 — the viewer's own money enters the grid; the label is the viewer's role, not the model's act.

elements.name: stake tile HOLDS ('how much it can hold at once')
elements.rationale: Stakes beat 4 of 4; its sub-line carries the restored 'at once' — the context window named in plain words.

elements.name: stream label 'THINKING IN TOKENS'
elements.rationale: The turn's thesis as a stage title — the one moment the piece names its own destination, in the slate register (a fact about the world, not a gold claim).

elements.name: the stream
elements.home: band y 690–890, 7 seeded mini-pieces flowing left→right
elements.rationale: Tokens in motion at scale: identical units, endlessly passing — the quadrillion made visible as traffic. Texture inside one element; the mini token piece rides its centre (the shared object), so the stream reads as made of the same unit the viewer just counted.

elements.name: bridge card — WD-04 'What Is Context?'
elements.rationale: Silent, after the close, over bed only: the referral the turn built ('the stream those tokens move in'). Packaging, never narration — the arc ends at the bookend; the card is the door, not a second ending.

elements.name: the word layer
elements.rationale: Word animation, never a caption plate: the narration's words in the stage's empty lower band, current word gold, principals held gold, the sentence assembling as it is spoken. Sound-off, the piece still reads.

qa_log: PASS 1 (16 frames, viewed): (1) ghost numeral + gold QUADRILLION compose the monument as designed; source + context lines land on their words. (2) DEFECT (fixed): word-span margins (.14em) were eaten by the current word's scale pop (1.14) — adjacent words touched ('tokensGoogle's', 'awhole', 'fourcharacters'); margins widened to .22em and the pop reduced to 1.07 — re-shot frames show clean gaps at every junction. (3) DEFECT (fixed): the question tile's first home (y 1252) overlapped the word band; moved to centre stage (y 688) over the receded ghost — the question now poses inside the number. (4) DEFECT (fixed): the lifted token piece overlapped the cut word; lift deepened (−145 px) and the word lowered (y 835) — the cut now plays in clear space. (5) DEFECT (fixed): the counter's verdict shared the numerals' line, shifting them off-centre until it appeared; verdict moved to its own centred row. (6) DEFECT (fixed): the mini piece's C7 sub-label wrapped outside its border; sub-label type reduced (19 px / .12em) — fits on one line at every state. (7) DEFECT (fixed): the expanded digits sat high in the ghost's mass; lowered to y 700 (the ghost's centre of mass).

PASS 2 (9 frames re-shot after fixes, viewed): all six fixes verified in frame; the count tableau (tiles + counter + verdict), the stakes grid mid-lighting, the stream with the mini piece riding its centre, the return monument and the bridge card all read as designed. The stream's flowing pieces cross the mini piece's plane — observed and accepted as depth (the piece and its label stay legible throughout).

ENGINE NOTE: two authoring defects were caught before first frames (an eid-map reference to id-only elements threw and froze the scene at its CSS state; a tile-row offset breached the safe zone) — both fixed and re-verified by screenshot diff (identical-hash frames exposed the freeze).
